label: copy step outputting original token 2 (input = orig token 1) in short sequences (L<=5)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost exclusively at recall_idx == 2 (step L+2, where the fed-back input is original token 1 and the model must output original token 2); 99.99% of activations and mass sit there. Strongly length-dependent: rate within that slot is ~8% at L=3, high at L=4-5 (L=4 carries 62% of mass, L=5 27%), and near zero for L>=6. Never fires in the original or delimiter phases or at any other recall position. Within the slot it fires on only ~47% of eligible steps; which ones depends diffusely on token identity: more likely when the first original token is a letter like e/w/c/f/y/b, the input is a letter (digits and repeated tokens lower the rate), and fewer digits in the sequence; top activations are 3-4 token all-letter sequences, often ending in v (e.g. e t v <DEL> e [t]). Those token preferences are spread across many tokens and could not be captured by a compact predicate.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the previous input (most: e, w, b, c, t, y; least: x, 1, i, h) and the current input token, by step (t=6: t, e, r, c; t=8: e, z, r, 2; t=7: r, e, t, 2); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=2, L=4 & t=6, L=5 & t=7.
